history.summary: Large 1,442sqft 3BR at Braddell MRT (280m), $2.4M / $1,664psf — a striking ~15% below the URA median ($1,967). Generous size, two-MRT access and a responsive MCST make this an efficient, well-priced D12 hold; the discount reflects the bay-window/balcony-heavy layout rather than a defect.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,664psf vs $1,967 URA median is a ~15% discount — the standout value in this batch on an absolute-PSF basis, driven by the large 1,442sqft format (price-per-foot compresses on big units). 134 transactions = liquid, reliable; 5.64%/yr CAGR is healthy. 280m to Braddell NS18 plus Toa Payoh within reach is a real transit/rental anchor. Reviews note responsive MCST and good maintenance. Caveats: $2.4M sits at the upper edge of the liquid band, and reviews flag thin soundproofing and bay-window/balcony space that inflates strata area — partly why PSF reads cheap. Net: large, central, MRT-fronting, fairly-to-cheaply priced. MMR 746 / on frontier supports.
red_flags: Reviews cite poor soundproofing between units
Bay windows / large balconies inflate strata area (PSF flatters the layout)
$2.4M near the top of the liquid price band; 99yr leasehold

280m to Braddell MRT plus second-MRT access (Toa Payoh) — strong liquidity

history.summary: A 1,442 sqft 3BR at $1,664 psf sits clearly below Trevista's verified 12-month range ($1,728-$2,197 psf, avg ~$2,042 across 134 deals), in a large, liquid, MRT-served RCR project — a genuine value entry on deep data.
history.rating_rationale: $2.4M / 1,442 sqft ($1,664 psf) is below the bottom of Trevista's last-12-month transaction band ($1,728-$2,197 psf, avg ~$2,042); even allowing that large 3BRs trade at lower psf than the pool, this is a real discount, and another 1,442 sqft unit is listed higher at $2.6M. The signal is well-supported: appreciation_txns=134 and psf_cohort_txns=8, so the -11.2% age-adj / -14.6% cohort discount is not thin-data noise. Trevista is a 590-unit project a few minutes from Braddell and Toa Payoh MRT in D12 (RCR, ~+3.5% forward realized), giving strong family-resale and rental liquidity. Per v3.4 priors I weight the verified value gap over the trailing 5.64% CAGR (story only). A large, well-located family unit bought below recent comps on deep data is a Buy; medium confidence because the discount partly reflects the larger-unit psf structure and lease decay (1999/2008-vintage 99yr).
red_flags: 99-yr leasehold (completed ~2011) — lease decay over a 5-7yr hold
Part of the cohort discount reflects normal large-unit psf compression, not pure bargain
$2.4M is a high absolute quantum, narrowing the buyer pool on exit
catalysts: Few minutes to Braddell (NSL) and Toa Payoh (NSL) MRT — city-fringe convenience
Large 590-unit project = strong, liquid resale and rental market for 3BR families
Established Toa Payoh estate amenities; consistent owner-occupier demand

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Trailing 5.64% CAGR (134 txns) is solid but treated as narrative, not a forward guarantee; the forward case is the verified sub-band entry price plus RCR drift, the value signal the backtest rewards.
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Large 3BR near two MRT lines rents readily to families; yield on a $2.4M quantum is modest, so this is a value-and-liquidity hold rather than a yield maximiser.
